thread.title_full: Multiple States Move to Ban Masks for ICE Agents - NewsBreak

author: John Baker
title: Multiple States Move to Ban Masks for ICE Agents - NewsBreak
text: Democratic-led states such as California, New York, Massachusetts, and Pennsylvania have advanced legislation to impose bans on face coverings and mandates for visible identification on federal immigration agents. The efforts aim to enhance transparency and curb the enforcement powers of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) due to ongoing concerns regarding its enforcement tactics. Supporters have argued that visible ID requirements are essential for public accountability and safety. Rep. Laura Friedman (D-CA) said, “I’ll keep fighting to pass commonsense legislation, like the No Masks for ICE Act, to keep our communities safe.” California’s No Secret Police Act, introduced by Sen. Scott Wiener and Sen. Jesse Arreguín, prohibits law enforcement officers from covering their faces, with exceptions for undercover operations or medical needs. The bill passed the state Senate Public Safety Committee but is expected to face legal challenges. New York’s MELT Act, introduced by Assemblymember Tony Simone, would ban most mask use by law enforcement and require visible ID, with violations treated as misdemeanors. Similar bills in Massachusetts and Pennsylvania target ICE tactics. DHS Spokeswoman Tricia McLaughlin said, “The men and women of ICE put their lives on the line every day to arrest violent criminal illegal aliens to protect and defend the lives of American citizens.” House Democrats introduced the No Anonymity in Immigration Enforcement Act, requiring ICE agents to wear identifiable gear during operations. Exceptions apply for imminent security threats and require supervisory review. Former ICE Director John Sandweg said, “If you’re getting arrested by an officer or agent in a mask, especially if at that point they’ve not yet identified themselves as a federal officer, it creates a risk of bystanders thinking, rushing in to help, which could create the risk of violence or harm caused to the bystanders.” Supporters of state bills argue that transparency is essential for accountability, while the White House has maintained that masks are necessary for agents’ safety amid increasing hostility. White House Spokesperson Abigail Jackson said, “ICE officers are being doxed, physically assaulted, and attacked—in some cases, their families are even being threatened. Instead of spending their time further demonizing heroic ICE officers, Democrat politicians should dial back the rhetoric and tell their supporters to stop attacking law enforcement.” John Baker covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
